summary: The @gyomu/schema package provides a robust, schema-driven foundation for domain modeling, validation, and error handling. It leverages the Effect ecosystem to enforce data integrity, standardize cross-layer communication, and automate the generation of CRUD patterns for business entities.
responsibilities: Define and maintain centralized domain entity schemas and their corresponding CRUD structures.
Standardize error handling through composable error traits, operational policies, and diagnostic context.
Provide advanced TypeScript source code analysis and structural metadata for documentation and introspection.
Implement consistent data conversion and validation utilities that bridge the gap between raw input and structured domain models.
Establish shared operational infrastructure for logging, retries, and result patterns.

capabilities.name: Domain Entity Modeling
capabilities.description: Enables the definition of business entities and the automatic derivation of comprehensive CRUD schemas, UI annotations, and validation logic.

capabilities.name: Structured Error Framework
capabilities.description: Provides a hierarchical error system with standardized contexts, behavioral traits, and retry policies for consistent failure reporting.

capabilities.name: Code Analysis Engine
capabilities.description: Offers rich structural metadata extraction for TypeScript symbols, types, and dependencies, facilitating code-aware tooling and documentation generation.

capabilities.name: Data Validation and Conversion
capabilities.description: Facilitates safe transformation of input data into validated models, including sophisticated error resolution and flattening of validation issues.

capabilities.name: Operational Infrastructure
capabilities.description: Provides essential utilities for system orchestration, including polling, logging, standardized result handling, and security-aware path resolution.

designDecisions: Adopts a schema-first approach where data structures act as the single source of truth for both validation and API/DB contracts.
Utilizes branded types for sensitive or structural identifiers (e.g., UserId) to enhance type safety and prevent logic errors.
Integrates heavily with the Effect framework for functional error handling, concurrency control, and service definition.
Employs a compositional pattern for error traits, allowing behavior to be injected dynamically into domain-specific error classes.
Favors automated generation of repetitive infrastructure code (like CRUD schemas) from minimal entity definitions to ensure consistency.
usageGuidance: Use the entity definition framework to generate CRUD schemas rather than manual construction, ensuring compliance with system-wide metadata requirements.
Always wrap external integrations and I/O operations using the provided error wrapping utilities to ensure failures are automatically enriched with proper operational context.
Leverage the provided Effect-based helpers for data conversion to ensure that schema validation results are handled in a predictable, type-safe manner.
When implementing new domain entities, utilize the existing field definitions to ensure consistency in audit fields and temporal data handling.
